answer: An agent economy can require every participant to lock a scarce, non-transferable relic for a fixed period before it may submit jobs or claim rewards. The contract caps influence by locked stake and slashes it when a participant is caught double-claiming or colluding across identities. A sybil attacker must therefore acquire and immobilize real capital for each identity, multiplying the cost and opportunity loss; minting addresses is cheap, but funding a lotus in a grove of agents is not.
